text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1: High tail latency and failed model cold starts observed in Dedicated VPC pool for tenant=sentinel. Error rate spike 12:34 UTC, 99th p50->p99 jump x8. Affected routes: /v1/chat and /v1/generate. Auto-fallback attempted to lighter variant but failures continued. Paging on-call.
ops_julie: seeing same in console traces — backend alloc OOMs on GPU nodes, KV cache thrash. Sentinel traffic is heavy peak. Repro window started ~12:30, still ongoing.
eng_marc: joining. Can you paste the node logs where the model process crashes? suspect mismatch between seq_len distribution and cache prefill causing mem blowup.
ops_julie: logs (sanitized):
```
[12:33:07] model_runner: alloc failed: 0x7f... size=1.2G
[12:33:07] kv_cache: invalidation loop, flushed prefixes=2300
[12:33:07] watchdog: process exited code=137
```
se_tomas: if KV cache churn is the culprit we should pin sentinel to a safe variant with smaller KV footprint and quantized kernels. Recommend temporary override to redwood/llama2-13b-safe-q8-v2 (verified smaller KV allocation) and disable prefix caching for tenant during mitigation.
ps_simone: pinged sentinel_oncall to confirm acceptable brief behavior change (slightly quieter completions). @sentinel_oncall ?
sentinel_oncall: confirmed — we prefer availability. Pinning to a safe variant for 2 hours is fine. Keep us posted.
infra_lee: I can apply tenant-level model override. Suggest steps:
1) create policy in console override UI (Tenant -> Policies -> Fallback)
2) apply via CLI for speed:
```
# apply temporary override for sentinel
redwood override apply --tenant sentinel \
  --model redwood/llama2-13b-safe-q8-v2 \
  --duration 2h \
  --reason \"mitigate OOMs during peak; small-KV safe variant\"
```
3) set route-level param `kv_cache.enabled=false` for sentinel routes while we watch metrics.
infra_lee: I'll run the CLI now.
eng_marc: while infra applies, prepare a canary test to validate latency and correctness on a subset of sentinel traffic. Use A/B 5% traffic to variant first.
infra_lee: applied override, returned id=ovr-7892, status=applied. Canary routing set to 5%.
ops_julie: metrics: within 4 minutes p99 reduced ~60%, error rate down to baseline. No more OOMs logged.
product_anya: customer SLA note — this is an allowed temporary operational mitigation. We'll document in post-incident note and send to sentinel account team.
ps_simone: great. Need to confirm if any regressions in output quality for sentinel prompts. @eng_marc can you run the eval set we hold for sentinel against the safe variant?
eng_marc: running quick eval (100 prompts). Initial drift small — BLEU-ish metrics down 1.6%, hallucination rate unchanged. Quality acceptable per PS acceptance.
se_tomas: next step: craft a durable tenant policy to prefer safe-variants when memory pressure on assigned pool > 70% or when model cold-start errors exceed threshold. Example policy payload:
```
{
  \"tenant\": \"sentinel\",
  \"trigger\": {
    \"pool_memory_percent\": \">70\",
    \"cold_start_errors\": \">5/min\"
  },
  \"action\": {
    \"pin_model\": \"redwood/llama2-13b-safe-q8-v2\",
    \"kv_cache.enabled\": false,
    \"notify\": [\"ops\",\"eng\",\"ps\"]
  },
  \"ttl\": \"manual\"
}
```
infra_lee: I'll enter this as a canary policy in the private control plane (needs review). We should also add an automated rollback after 2h unless overridden.
ops_julie: handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. @infra_lee please monitor the override ID ovr-7892. If errors resurge, escalate paging to eng-marc.
infra_lee: ack. Setting alert rule: if sentinel p99 > 2s for 3 minutes OR error rate > 2% then page eng_marc + ops.
product_anya: customer comms: I'll send a short note: \"We applied a temporary model pin to maintain availability; working on durable policy. No data was routed outside your VPC.\"
sentinel_oncall: appreciate the quick action. Please keep us in the loop if you plan to push any permanent changes.
eng_marc: follow-ups:
- postmortem to include root cause (KV cache + seq_len mismatch), why auto-fallback failed, and improve auto-fallback heuristics to try quantized-safe variants first for memory pressure.
- add more conservative default for tenant pin rules on Dedicated pools with small node counts.
- add a preflight check in rollout code to avoid hot-cache thrash.
ops_julie: creating incident page now and will assign owners. Severity remains P1 until we close or stabilize for 1 hour.
incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0315-271; severity=P1; owners=[ops_julie, eng_marc, infra_lee]; timeline link: https://console.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0315-271
infra_lee: note: override ovr-7892 set to expire at +2h (1839003323). I'll prepare a decay plan: if metrics stable for 90m we can lift manually.
ps_simone: add a follow-up PS verification after 4 hours to sign off with sentinel.
ops_julie: handing off to night oncall @infra_lee for monitoring/rollback. I'm putting a runbook note: \"If errors return, increase canary to 25% only after eng_marc confirms stability; otherwise rollback override and fail open to hosted pool.\"
infra_lee: ack handoff. Monitoring dashboard pinned in channel. Will update last_message_ts when I close or escalate.
product_anya: also flag this customer for a dedicated capacity review — they might need an additional reserved node for peak.
sentinel_oncall: thanks team, we will review billing and capacity options with your account team.
eng_marc: good job. We'll debrief in the postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC. Action items assigned in the incident doc.
ops_julie: thanks everyone. Closing my window now. :hand:
__comment: This thread simulates a live incident coordination for a customer-specific model override in a Dedicated VPC environment.
